scout.purpose: Small settings, typed configuration, and larger opaque files need storage APIs matched to size, schema, update, integrity, and sharing requirements.
scout.realWorldUse: Theme settings, sort order, sync preferences, downloaded documents, import/export, and cache files should not be forced into one relational database.
scout.outcome: Choose Preferences or typed DataStore, apply atomic updates and corruption policy, and select internal, cache, or shared file locations.

blocks.text: DataStore exposes a Flow of current data and an atomic updateData transformation. Preferences DataStore stores typed values under keys without a predefined schema; typed DataStore uses a serializer and immutable schema model such as Protocol Buffers or reviewed JSON. Create one instance for a file and inject it. DataStore suits small datasets and does not provide partial relational queries, joins, or referential integrity; use Room for large or relational data.

blocks.caption: Reads distinguish I/O from corruption and updates publish one immutable transactional value.

sections.title: Preferences and typed stores trade schema flexibility

blocks.text: Updates serialize through DataStore so concurrent transformations do not lose changes. The transform may run more than once and must avoid external side effects. IOException during reading may support a default or retry policy, while CorruptionException should follow a deliberate corruption handler rather than catch-all data loss. Typed schema evolution preserves field numbers and defaults. SharedPreferences migration should happen once and remain tested until no supported install requires it.

blocks.caption: Reads distinguish I/O from corruption and updates publish one immutable transactional value.

blocks.title: DataStore is not a small database replacement
blocks.text: It serializes one small logical dataset without relational query or partial update.

sections.title: Files require location, lifetime, and atomic replacement policy

blocks.text: Internal files are private to the app and removed on uninstall; cache files can be deleted by the system and must be reconstructable. User-selected export uses Storage Access Framework destinations rather than broad storage paths. For an app-owned document, write a temporary file, flush and close it, then atomically rename when supported so interruption does not replace a good file with a partial one. Validate size and format, close streams with use, and never store relational query data as one giant JSON preference.

Production data work must remain correct after interruption and repetition. Define the source of truth, stable operation identity, transaction boundary, cancellation behaviour, and the state shown before remote confirmation. Exercise empty and stale data, malformed input, duplicate delivery, simultaneous callers, process death, schema upgrade, storage pressure, and connectivity restoration where relevant. Use pure unit tests for mapping and conflict policy, real Room or DataStore instances for persistence contracts, MockWebServer for protocol behaviour, and WorkManager test APIs for durable scheduling. Logs must reveal operation state without exposing tokens, user content, or personal identifiers. A future engineer should be able to explain which component owns every row, cursor, credential, retry, and final user-visible outcome.

steps.label: Define contract
steps.detail: Name authority, identity, lifetime, failure, cancellation, and recovery.

steps.label: Persist intent
steps.detail: Commit user-visible state or queued work before unreliable boundaries.

steps.label: Execute
steps.detail: Perform the smallest idempotent or transactional operation.

steps.label: Reconcile
steps.detail: Merge authoritative outcome and resolve conflicts deliberately.

steps.label: Verify
steps.detail: Test interruption, recreation, migration, duplication, and offline recovery.

blocks.title: Do not create multiple DataStore instances for one file
blocks.text: Competing owners break its single-process consistency contract.

inspect.title: Move the article list out of DataStore
walkthrough: A growing relational dataset is rewritten as one opaque settings value.
Partial query, indexing, migrations, and referential integrity become difficult.
Store articles in Room and reserve DataStore for small configuration.
inspect.expectedOutput: Settings updates remain small while Room queries article data efficiently.

trap_check.mistake: Treating a cache file as durable user data.
trap_check.why: The system may delete cache storage under pressure.
trap_check.fix: Use durable internal or user-selected storage for irreplaceable content.

trap_check.mistake: Adding a retry, cache, or abstraction without naming the failure contract.
trap_check.why: The implementation hides ambiguity while duplicate, stale, or lost outcomes remain possible.
trap_check.fix: Write the invariant and an interruption test before introducing machinery.

challenge_intro.task: Implement typed sync settings, corruption handling, one-time migration, cached thumbnails, and atomic user-selected article export with tested interruption.
challenge_intro.successLooksLike: One DataStore instance owns its file. Cache and durable file lifetimes are distinct. Interrupted export never replaces a valid file with partial data.

recall.answer: An atomic transformation of current DataStore value.

recall.prompt: When should Room be used instead?
recall.answer: For large, relational, or partially queried datasets.
